interpretation: Sellars, speaking as a philosopher, says that the common-sense world of physical objects in Space and Time is unreal, or less paradoxically that in the dimension of describing and explaining the world science is the measure of all things. Read as the methodological thesis only. The same paragraph says the scientific picture replaces the common-sense one; it does not say that whatever exists is spatiotemporal, and it denies the reality of the common-sense framework of objects located in Space and enduring through Time, so it is not N1.
attribution: The passage states that in the dimension of describing and explaining the world science is the measure of all things, of what is that it is and of what is not that it is not, which is the premise.
